operating_notes.text: The bank inaugurated a new divisional office in Tiruppur, where it operates 37 branches.
Q4FY26 net profit stood at ₹724.96 Cr on total income of ₹3,519.45 Cr.
Fixed rate loan book increased to 29% at the end of March '26 from 23% in December.
Revised MCLR rates effective May 22, 2026, with overnight at 8.65%, one-month at 8.55%, three-month at 8.85%, six-month at 9.00%, and one-year at 9.15%.
CIT(A) partly allowed the bank's appeal against a ₹40.34 Cr income tax demand for AY 2022-23; the bank expects the entire demand to be set aside.
Launched four Visa credit card variants — Aura (Platinum), Samara (Signature), Altura (Infinite) and Eternis (Infinite) — first offered to existing customers via the KVB DLite app.
As of March 31, 2026, total business was ₹2,14,420 crore: deposits ₹1,15,666 crore and advances ₹98,754 crore, across 901 branches.
Gold loans are about 30% of advances against an internal cap of 30-35%; agriculture gold loans are 92% of the agri portfolio with LTV of 63.7% (agri) and 56.83% (non-agri).
ECLGS: 2,232 commercial applications with ₹140 Cr disbursed in Q2 and 54 corporate applications with ₹80 Cr disbursed; ₹10 Cr was disbursed in Q1.
FCNR(B) deposit base is about USD 130 million before the new scheme, with pricing at 7% and an aim to double or triple it.
Sep-2026: capital adequacy ratio (Basel III) 17.97% against 18.61% a year earlier; provision coverage ratio 96.13%.
Sep-2026: co-lending gross outstanding ₹98,036 lakh across 9 partners at a weighted average rate of 18.62%, with standard loans ₹94,097 lakh and NPAs ₹3,939 lakh.
Sep-2026: projects under implementation 39 accounts with ₹87,599 lakh outstanding, up from 33 accounts and ₹81,105 lakh at the start of the quarter.
Jewel loans were ₹32,153 Cr, 29% of advances, against an internal cap of 35% of advances or 32% of total exposure.
Agriculture gold loans carry 67% LTV and non-agri gold loans 59% LTV as of 30 September 2026.
Recovery from written-off accounts was ₹82 Cr in Q2FY27, and the bank holds a pool of about ₹2,500 Cr for future recoveries.

timeline.summary: Karur Vysya Bank inaugurated a new divisional office in Tiruppur to support MSMEs and exporters.
Q4FY26 results (standalone): interest earned ₹2,903.65 Cr (+15.4% YoY), net profit ₹724.96 Cr (+41.2% YoY).
Karur Vysya Bank’s Board, led by **Srinivasarao IVI (Deputy General Manager)**, recommended a **final dividend of ₹2.60 per equity share (130%)** for FY2026 on May 7, 2026, pending AGM approval.
Karur Vysya Bank reported Q4FY26 standalone net profit of ₹725 Cr and recommended a 130% dividend.
Karur Vysya Bank revised its Marginal Cost of Funds Based Lending Rates effective May 22, 2026.
Karur Vysya Bank received a Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) order partly allowing its appeal against a ₹40.34 Cr AY 2022-23 demand, and will challenge it further.
Karur Vysya Bank launched a four-card premium Visa credit card portfolio (Aura, Samara, Altura, Eternis), rolled out first to existing customers.
ICRA reaffirmed the ICRA A1+ rating on Karur Vysya Bank's ₹10,000 Cr Certificate of Deposit Programme on June 5, 2026.
Shri B Ramesh Babu (MD & CEO), Shri Sankar B (ED), and Shri R Ramshankar (CFO) attended ICICI Securities’ ‘India Rising: The Next Chapter’ meet on June 08, 2026, at Grand Hyatt, Mumbai.
On its 20 July 2026 Q1FY27 call, Karur Vysya Bank reported net profit of ₹756 Cr (up 45% YoY), NIM of 4.26% and GNPA of 0.74%, and kept FY27 NIM guidance at 3.7-3.8%.
Q2FY27 results (standalone): interest earned ₹3,235.4 Cr (+15.2% YoY), net profit ₹787.69 Cr (+37.2% YoY).
On 15 October 2026, Karur Vysya Bank approved the allotment of 14,442 equity shares under its ESOS 2018 scheme for senior management variable pay.
On its 15 October 2026 Q2FY27 call, Karur Vysya Bank guided FY27 credit growth at 18-20% and NIM above 4%, after holding NIM at 4.26% and lifting PAT 37% YoY to ₹788 Cr.

watchlist.text: Shareholder approval for dividend at the AGM

status_history.evidence: GNPA fell to 0.69% at Sep-2026 from 0.74% at Jun-2026

watchlist.response: MD cited NPA upgrades and provision releases below PPOP, non-fund business income, and 10-15 bps each from CASA in cost of deposits and other income to offset the decline
watchlist.text: Analyst asked what will replace write-off recoveries, which contributed 15-20% of profitability and are shrinking about 20% a year

watchlist.response: MD gave only near-term visibility of 4% plus for next quarter and deferred the full-year view to after Q2, saying the guidance was given only two months ago
watchlist.text: Analyst pressed for a realistic full-year margin number given NIM is running far above the 3.7-3.8% guidance

watchlist.response: CFO said it would be premature to indicate a normalized credit cost, citing portfolio mix dependence, with 10-11 months still available
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for normalized credit cost under ECL over the next year

watchlist.response: Management said working capital utilisation has stayed at 76-79% for 1-1.5 years, US-export textile clients use only 55-56%, and it sees little capex; growth is coming from fresh acquisitions and takeovers.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the split of corporate/SME demand between working capital drawdown, genuine capex and loan takeovers.

watchlist.response: Management said yields may fall 3-4 bps and it cannot promise 4.26% retention, but assured NIM above 4% for the next two quarters.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked whether NIM would trend down from 4.26% given rising deposit costs and corporate focus.

watchlist.response: Management said it did not have the figure readily and would share it later, which was evasive.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the AFS reserves at end-Q2 and end-Q1.

watchlist.response: Management gave components (₹100 Cr ECL, ₹100 Cr contingency, ₹25 Cr this quarter, restructuring 41% of ₹373 Cr) but did not confirm the analyst's total split.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the breakup of the 1.65% provisions (ECL, RSA, West Asia, standard assets).
